hypothesis: If bivalve growth lines are a coaxial family generated by a direction-dependent growth rate about the umbo, then on one valve the successive lines are scaled copies of a single curve through the umbo, and that family fits better than concentric circles about a centre that need not be the umbo; in the simplest case, Anomia, the shared curve is a circle through the umbo.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Photographs, not engravings, are the only admissible images: the frozen Commons file titles listed under planned_datasets, each already confirmed as JPEG or PNG under CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA, and none of them in the categories Illustrated Index of British Shells or Iconographia Zoologica. The Sowerby plates of Lima subauriculata and Solen pellucidus were located and are excluded because they are engravings. For each photograph the shell is the largest region whose colour differs from the corner background; the umbo is the outline point of maximum curvature. Growth lines are radial-ridge traces inside the shell that each span at least 100 degrees with at least 30 points. A valve qualifies with at least 4 such lines. A verdict other than inconclusive requires at least 6 qualifying valves of which at least 2 are Anomia. Radial RMSE is computed per line after dividing by that line's median radius. The coaxial model is r = t_i f(theta) with one shared f and a scale t_i per line. The concentric model is circles about one centre searched over the outline's bounding box. The circle-through-umbo model is r = t_i cos(theta - theta0) with theta0 shared. The claim is supported if the coaxial RMSE is lower than the concentric RMSE on at least 75% of qualifying valves, the median ratio of those RMSEs is at most 0.80, and the median Anomia ratio of circle-through-umbo RMSE to the best Thompson-ellipse RMSE is at most 1.25.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. The claim is refuted if, on a sample that meets the size rule, the coaxial RMSE is higher than the concentric RMSE on at least 75% of valves or the median ratio is at least 1.25, or the median Anomia circle-to-ellipse RMSE ratio is at least 2. Results between the pass and fail thresholds are mixed. If no valve yields four growth lines the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. If some valves qualify but fewer than six, or fewer than two are Anomia, the verdict is inconclusive with reason underpowered. Lima and Tellinidae ellipse axis ratios are reported and do not enter the verdict. No Solen photograph was in the frozen list, so the Solen axis-ratio sentence is untested.

test_contract.expected_observation: Successive growth lines on a valve are scaled copies of one curve based at the umbo, closer to that coaxial family than to concentric circles, and Anomia's curve is nearly a circle through the umbo.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Growth lines fit concentric circles about a free centre better than any single curve scaled from the umbo, or Anomia's lines are at least twice as far from a circle through the umbo as from an ellipse.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Openly licensed photographs of real valves in which commarginal growth lines are visible, not engravings, not Thompson's figures, and not sclerochronological cross-sections (those are cuts through the shell thickness, not the surface family the claim describes). The valve and the umbo must be segmentable without being placed by hand.
test_contract.inference_method: Automatic ridge traces in polar coordinates about the curvature umbo; radial RMSE of a shared angular template against concentric circles and, for Anomia, against Thompson's circle-through-the-origin. Thresholds are those in pass_criterion and fail_criterion.

interpretation: Thompson's equation r(theta, t) = t f(theta) places every growth line through the umbo, so the lines are coaxial rather than concentric. f(theta) = cos theta is the circular case he assigns to Anomia; the ellipse formula he prints is the case he assigns to Lima (vertical axis about twice the transverse) and to Solen pellucidus (transverse axis three to four times the vertical). Tellina is named with the elliptical figures and is included as Tellinidae. Limatula is the current genus for the file-shells Thompson called Lima. Only the coaxial-versus-concentric contrast and the Anomia circle enter the verdict; the Lima axis ratio is descriptive because the frozen photograph list has no Solen valve to pair with it.
